prompt: Mark here. We're adding online holds and waitlists for physical books and e-books across the county library service. I've gathered all the documents in this folder – circulation policies, branch info, patron survey, last month's holds data, e-book vendor license, board memo, accessibility statement, meeting notes, etc. I need you to write up the requirements for the new system. Focus on what it should do for patrons and staff, policy rules librarians know, and constraints from the board and technical team. End the file with a ```json block of the form {"requirements": [{"id": "R1", "text": "..."}], "assumptions": ["..."]}. Put it in docs/requirements.md.

facts.answer: After the board review, the final hold limits are: regular cards 12 items, student cards 15 items during school year, senior cards 10 items, children's cards 5 items, institutional cards 20 items with manager approval over 10.
The pickup window is 7 days for all branches except North Hill which gets 10 days due to limited hours, and Central which stays at 7 days but allows after-hours pickup lockers.
For children's cards under 12, parents must receive separate notifications by default, and can opt out only in person at the branch with ID verification.
E-book waitlists for One Copy One User titles have a 24-hour checkout window after notification, not 48 hours as in the vendor summary, and patrons get one automatic renewal if no one is waiting.

Notification channels priority: email primary, SMS backup for holds ready, phone call only for seniors who opt in and for institutional holds. All notifications must include pickup branch and deadline.

The fines waiver starting March 1 applies only to holds placed after that date. Existing fines from before March 1 will still be collected but patrons can appeal for waiver if they use the new system within 60 days.

WCAG 2.1 AA compliance is required at launch for core hold placement and management. Advanced features like analytics dashboard have 6-month grace period but must meet basic accessibility immediately.
All physical branches launch together in Phase 1. Bookmobile is Phase 2, scheduled for August 2024. School delivery service is excluded entirely – stays manual.

scriptedUser.defaultReply: I'm not sure, use your judgement.

rubric.criterion: Requirements show understanding of both patron needs and staff workflows, not just restating documents. Fail: the requirements repeat the vendor summary, including the 48-hour e-book window the board changed, or treat every branch the same. Partial: they use the final rules, but cover only patron actions or only staff actions. Pass: they use the final board limits (regular 12, student 15 in the school year, senior 10, children's 5, institutional 20 with manager approval over 10), the pickup window of 7 days with 10 days at North Hill and after-hours lockers at Central, the 24-hour e-book checkout window with one automatic renewal if no one waits, and set out the staff steps (manager approval, children's-card parent notices, fines waiver only for holds placed after March 1). Where the folder disagrees with itself (the senior 10-day pickup and the teen limit in policy/circulation.md, waitlists listed for Phase 2 in the board memo, COPPA under 13 against children's cards under 12), either reading is acceptable when the requirement says which source it follows; do not mark a reasonable call down. (code cannot check this because it requires judgment of the document, not only a pattern)

There is a clear distinction between mandatory requirements and optional enhancements. Fail: all items sit in one list with no must or optional marking. Partial: some items are labelled, but board constraints and technical constraints are mixed with wishes, or the optional items are unmarked. Pass: board rules, accessibility compliance, notification content (pickup branch and deadline) and the email-first channel order (SMS backup, phone call only for opted-in seniors and institutional holds) are marked mandatory, and each optional enhancement is listed separately and marked optional. (code cannot check this because it requires judgment of the document, not only a pattern)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the vendor and board differences it settled by assumption stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/requirements.md was written. Partial: it names docs/requirements.md and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the vendor and board differences it settled by assumption. Pass: it names docs/requirements.md and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the vendor and board differences it settled by assumption still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

items.note: The prompt requests requirements for patrons and staff from the folder and defines only the output format; it supplies no prescribed elicitation method or misleading solution direction.
fixture/policy, fixture/board, fixture/accessibility and fixture/ebooks provide source policies, including deliberate disagreements, but no final requirements document or completed behavior list.

Hidden grounded paths all exist in fixture, and the final card, pickup, notification, e-book, fines, accessibility and rollout decisions are stated in task.json scriptedUser; rubric R1 and R2 reward those outcomes and source-qualified conflict handling.

A competent developer can use the policy and board documents plus the scripted clarifications to write the requirements, and hidden checks accept alternate wording, source choices, ordering and document structure.
